newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 30.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Senate and the House of Representatives finally agreed on Wednesday on a compromise 1997 national budget which is 3.45 billion pesos less than President Fidel Ramos' proposed 476-billion peso proposal. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- The Makati regional trial court on Wednesday entered a not guilty plea for Zamboanga del Norte congressman Romeo Jalosjos who is accused of statutory rape of an 11-year old school girl. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER, THE PHILIPPINE JOURNAL)

- Energy Secretary Francisco Viray gave an assurance on Wednesday that oil prices increases will be kept to their minimum once full deregulation of the oil sector takes effect next week. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- Philippine gross national product grew by 6.8 percent last year compared with five percent in 1995, Economic Planning Secretary Cielito Habito said. (BUSINESS WORLD)
- Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co's unaudited net income in 1996 rose 43 percent to 5.003 billion pesos (BUSINESS WORLD).

- San Miguel Corp said its net income increased by four percent to 6.09 billion pesos in 1996 from 5.84 billion last year. Excluding non-recurring items, however, net income dropped 11 percent to 5.26 billion pesos from 5.38 billion (ALL PAPERS).
